q: Calculate the expected number of copies after 10 cycles if every molecule doubled in every cycle.
Calculate the measured copies at 10 cycles as a percentage of the expected number.
Explain why the number of copies levels off after about 30 cycles.
Primers and nucleotides are used up; the polymerase slowly loses activity after many heating cycles; and the many copies pair with each other instead of with primers.
Calculate the time for 35 cycles, and explain why each cycle starts at about 95 °C.
35 × 3 = 105 minutes. At 95 °C the hydrogen bonds between the strands break, so the strands separate and can be copied.
Sample B started with 1000 copies. Estimate how many fewer cycles B needs to reach 8 million copies.
B has 100 times more to start. 100 is about 2^6.6, so about 7 fewer cycles (about 13 instead of 20).
